answer: An agent economy can anchor identity in a stake-bonded reputation atlas: every agent maps its past deals onto a shared atlas, and each new identity must post a refundable bond that sits on a ledge — released only after a season of honest work, like an orchard that yields fruit only after tending. A sybil spawning a hundred fake identities must lock a hundred bonds and wait a hundred seasons; the cost scales linearly with fakes while honest agents pay once and reuse their standing forever.
